report.answer_text:
The most recent example is Justice Dalveer Bhandari of India.
He became a judge of the Supreme Court of India on 28 October 2005.[1]
He served there for about seven years and resigned in 2012.[2]
He was then appointed a judge of the International Court of Justice.[2]
In 2017 he was re-elected to a nine-year term beginning on 6 February 2018.[3]
He sat on the ICJ bench that decided the Kulbhushan Jadhav case.[2]
Other Indian jurists have also served on the ICJ. Four Indians have served on the ICJ: Sir Benegal Rau (1952–1953), Justice Nagendra Singh (1973–1988, President 1985–1988), Justice R.S. Pathak (1989–1991) and Justice Dalveer Bhandari (2012–present).[4] Nagendra Singh was not a Supreme Court judge. Pathak was, and he was also Chief Justice of India.
Bhandari's current term runs out in early 2027. I didn't find confirmed results for the November 2026 election, so check the ICJ or UN websites for the latest.
If you meant a judge from another country, tell me which one and I'll look into it.

quotes.text: India has had four judges on the International Court of Justice bench since 1946.
Sir Benegal Narsing Rau served briefly on the bench from 1952 until his death in November 1953.

Justice Nagendra Singh, a former Chief Justice of India and Secretary to the President, served on the ICJ from 1973 to 1988. He was elected Vice-President in 1976 and elevated to President of the Court from 1985 to 1988
Justice R. S. Pathak, a former Chief Justice of India, served on the bench from 1989 to 1991 in the unexpired term of Nagendra Singh.
Justice Dalveer Bhandari, a former Judge of the Supreme Court of India, was first elected to the ICJ in April 2012

pages.quote_reason: The quotes back the four Indian judges and the dates for Rau, Singh (including his presidency), and Pathak, but for Bhandari they show only that he was first elected in April 2012, not that his service runs to the present.
pages.page_reason: The page's FAQ and Indian Judges section state that four Indians served on the ICJ, with exactly these names and date ranges (Rau 1952–1953, Nagendra Singh 1973–1988 with President 1985–1988, Pathak 1989–1991, Bhandari 2012–present), so the claim matches the page.
